title: PixelRNN, PixelCNN & WaveNet
blurb: Raster-scan images, masked and dilated convolutions

hook.title: Reading with a flashlight
hook.text: A convolution is a small **flashlight** sliding across the page. For image generation, we may only shine it on pixels already painted (above and to the left), so we tape over the rest: a **masked convolution**. For audio we need to see far into the past without enormous flashlights, so the beam **skips**: layer 1 looks at neighbours, layer 2 at every 2nd sample, layer 3 every 4th. That's a **dilated** convolution; a handful of layers sees seconds of sound.
hook.recall: Remember the flashlight: masking keeps it from lighting the future, dilation lets a few layers see far into the past, and convolutions can all run in parallel, unlike a pixel-by-pixel RNN.

explore.intro: Two tabs: dilated 1-D (WaveNet) and a 2-D masked convolution (PixelCNN).
tasks: WaveNet tab: set 4 layers. Compare the receptive field with and without dilation.
PixelCNN tab: which pixels are yellow, and why those?
explore.takeaway: Masked conv keeps raster-scan order; dilation grows the receptive field quickly. PixelCNN gives similar quality to PixelRNN but trains much faster.

questions.prompt: What do masked convolutions in PixelCNN preserve?
questions.explanation: The mask zeroes out weights on pixels not yet generated.
